## Oct 23 Recap: A Sample Size of One, Done Right

In sabermetrics, we're taught to resist small sample theater. But when your singular pick converts at 100% efficiency, you take the W and update your priors accordingly. The model posted a clean 1-0 slate on October 23rd, with Milwaukee doing exactly what the regression indicators suggested they would against Tampa Bay.

## The Milwaukee Blueprint Executed

The 55% confidence interval on Milwaukee wasn't screaming conviction, but the underlying metrics supported home field advantage and run differential expectations. When you're calibrating probability estimates, a 55% edge that converts is worth exactly as much as a 95% edge—it's one unit of expected value realized. The Brewers' pitching staff continues to suppress quality contact at elite rates, and American Family Field's park factors played precisely to expectation.

## Oct 24 Preview: Rematch Dynamics and Pitcher Variance

Tomorrow brings an immediate rematch, which introduces fascinating questions about sample autocorrelation. Do yesterday's results inform today's probability distribution? The model says: barely. We're projecting Milwaukee again, but confidence has actually *decreased* to 50%—a true coin flip with microscopic edge.

## Pitcher Matchup: Rasmussen vs Henderson

Drew Rasmussen brings Tampa Bay's trademark command-over-stuff philosophy. His walk rate metrics remain elite, but the Brewers' disciplined approach at the plate (top-10 in chase rate) neutralizes that edge. Logan Henderson counters with swing-and-miss upside—his whiff percentage grades above average, particularly on breaking balls.

The WAR projections here are essentially symmetrical. Neither pitcher provides multi-win separation talent, which pushes us back toward home field advantage as the deciding micro-edge. At 50% confidence, this is a model recommendation that admits uncertainty—exactly the kind of intellectual honesty that separates long-term profitable handicapping from narrative-driven guesswork.

Expect tight run environment. Expect bullpen leverage situations. Expect one-run game variance to determine outcome.

## The Bottom Line

Oct 23 delivered efficient conversion of modest probability advantage. Oct 24 presents a true test of process over results—when the model says "50%," it's acknowledging that coin flips exist in baseball. We're backing Milwaukee based on microscopic park factor and bullpen depth advantages, but make no mistake: this is variance territory.

Stay process-focused. Trust the regression. See you after first pitch.
